cases.prompt: What happened in crypto this week, and what can I do on Hyperliquid?
cases.expectedUserOutcome: Answer both halves: use current external evidence for the news summary and Avalon's own capability truth for what the user can do, keeping those sources distinct.
cases.actualResponse:
Here's what's been moving in crypto this week:

**Geopolitical shockwaves.** Crypto prices tumbled early in the week as U.S. airstrikes against Iranian targets reignited, with Iran retaliating by attacking U.S. military bases. Bitcoin and Ethereum both sold off sharply on the risk-off move [3](https://finance.yahoo.com/personal-finance/investing/article/bitcoin-and-ethereum-prices-today-wednesday-september-2-2026-crypto-prices-tumble-as-iran-war-reignites-112639522.html).

**Bitcoin ETF inflows surged.** Despite the volatility, U.S. Bitcoin ETFs recorded their largest single-day inflow since January — $731 million — bringing three-week inflows to $3.8 billion, the strongest stretch of the year [1](https://www.theblock.co/directory/archive/2026/9)[6](https://cointelegraph.com/). Combined Bitcoin and Ethereum fund inflows topped $2 billion for the week [4](https://x.com/calebandbrown/status/2094589491960861104).

**Macro catalysts loom.** The September FOMC meeting (Sept 15–16) is the month's biggest event. Futures markets price a 34.8% chance of a rate *hike* rather than a cut, and past 2026 Fed decisions have triggered bearish Bitcoin pivots. CPI data on Sept 11 will shape expectations heading into the meeting [5](https://www.bitrue.com/blog/crypto-market-events-this-month). A surprise nonfarm payrolls print also sent Bitcoin back below $80K [6](https://cointelegraph.com/).

**Hyperliquid enters the spotlight.** President Trump publicly said he wants Hyperliquid to enter the U.S., raising questions about how that could unfold [8](https://www.theblock.co/directory/archive/2026). Coinbase also filed with the SEC to list 24/7 equity perpetuals [1](https://www.theblock.co/directory/archive/2026/9).

**Institutional adoption continues.** Standard Chartered launched institutional spot crypto trading (BTC and ETH) in the UAE, becoming the first global systemically important bank to offer the service in the Gulf [9](https://www.reuters.com/markets/cryptocurrency/). South Korea announced plans to tokenize all types of securities starting in 2027 [1](https://www.theblock.co/directory/archive/2026/9).

**Lightning vulnerability found.** AI-assisted researchers uncovered a critical Bitcoin Lightning Network vulnerability [4](https://x.com/calebandbrown/status/2094589491960861104).

---

**What you can do on Hyperliquid through Avalon:**

- **Trade perpetuals** — go long or short on crypto (BTC, ETH, SOL, etc.) or equity/commodity reference contracts (NVDA, TSLA, GOLD, SP500, etc.) with leverage. These are perpetual futures providing price exposure only, not actual shares.
- **Backtest strategies** — design a strategy, run it against historical Hyperliquid data, and see how it performs before risking real money.
- **Set up live agents** — once you're happy with a strategy, deploy it as an autonomous agent that trades on your behalf within limits you set. You fund and authorize the agent once; it then trades inside its cap on its own.
- **Watch-only agents** — monitor any market with a read-only agent, nothing at risk.

Note: Avalon supports Hyperliquid perpetuals, not Hyperliquid spot. Liquidity on equity perpetuals is thinner than on the major crypto perps.
